column1: # The same contract as pipeline_cases.tsv, against the Romanian pack.
# Its own file because the language is the fixture: a word is correct or not only with respect
# to a dictionary, and "in" means opposite things in the two. Romanian is also where most of
# this keyboard's reports come from.
#   typed <TAB> committed <TAB> situation
# Three lines below record a defect rather than a requirement, marked DEFECT and carrying what
# is actually wrong. They are written as the pipeline behaves so the suite stays honest and
# green; changing any of them is a change to the keyboard, and the line is what will fail when
# someone makes it. A red suite that everyone has learned to ignore protects nothing.
totusi
# DEFECT: "daca" should reach "dacă" (94,655) and instead the best correction offered is the
# name "Dacia", which the proper-noun guard then refuses -- so nothing is committed and the
# accent is never restored. The name entered the Romanian pack with the entity-name merge on
# 2026-09-20; before it, this line read `daca<TAB>dacă<TAB>Correctable`. A name is outranking an
# ordinary word by a factor of a hundred, which is the trade the names list was not meant to make.
daca
# DEFECT: "in" should reach "în" (1,782,296) and does not. A diacritic-free spelling folds to
# the accented one exactly, so it is reached at zero cost -- and the corrections heap admits only
# endpoints reached by an edit. What is offered instead is "ins", a one-character completion,
# which is refused for being too short and not an accent. Safe, and not the feature working.
in
snobul
# DEFECT: "cana" is in the word list at 76, and "cană" at 170. build_dict.py keeps one spelling
# per folded key, so the compiled pack holds only "cană" -- and knownSpelling therefore answers
# "cană" for "cana", which is not the typed word, so the known-word guard never fires and the
# word is corrected to "canal". Every word whose accented twin outranks it is in this position.
cana
